punchline: Almost every app has some benefit, which is exactly why 'any benefit' is the wrong test.
thirty_sec: In Digital Minimalism, Cal Newport criticizes the 'any-benefit mindset': adopting tools because they offer some benefit, while ignoring their cost in time and attention. His alternative: focus online time on a few carefully chosen activities that strongly support what you value, and happily miss out on the rest. He points to the Amish, who evaluate each technology against their values before adopting it.
question: What deep value is each of your most-used apps actually serving?
